proposals: DPIIT should publish PLI disbursements state by state for every scheme, with applications, approvals, sanctions and payments shown as a funnel like the Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund dashboard, so the single most useful missing number in the incentive debate exists in a government source.

DPIIT should add a project-location column to state-wise FDI statistics, as NCAER recommended in 2016, and publish a methodology note in place of “Not applicable”, so Jio Platforms or Reliance Retail inflows are no longer credited to states only because of a registered office.

DPIIT should extend its top-five-sector FDI synopsis beyond its top five FDI states to every state, including Odisha, Andhra Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh, so a sector-adjusted manufacturing comparison can be made for the states that lead on implemented investment.

The industries departments of Maharashtra and Karnataka should publish an annual incentive-disbursal series as Rajasthan does for RIPS, and Gujarat should remove the login gate on its Large and Mega track dashboard, so promised and paid incentives can be compared across major states.

The governments of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh should publish their pending industrial-incentive claims by year of claim, with a dated clearance schedule, so arrears put at ₹3,736 crore and ₹3,000–5,000 crore are tracked against a public commitment rather than reported only through overlapping estimates.
